summary.name: Driftwall
summary.one_liner: Driftwall is a free, open-source macOS app that plays any .mp4 or .mov video as a looping live wallpaper behind desktop icons, on every display.
use_cases: Play a looping video behind desktop icons on a Mac
Use different videos on each monitor
Rotate a playlist of wallpaper videos on a timer
Save battery by pausing video wallpaper on battery power
Set a 4K video as desktop background
summary.what_it_does: Driftwall plays any .mp4 or .mov file, including 4K, as a seamless loop behind the desktop icons. It can show the same video on all displays or a different one on each, and picks up monitors that are plugged in later. The video pauses when a fullscreen app is in front or windows cover the desktop, and resumes when the desktop is visible again. Several videos can be lined up with a timer and optional shuffle. It runs from the menu bar, pauses on battery by default, and states that it never connects to the internet and has no tracking.
notable: Runs offline; states it never connects to the internet and has no tracking
Pauses video when fullscreen apps or covering windows hide the desktop, and on battery by default
Per-display videos with support for hot-plugged monitors
MIT licensed with code on GitHub; listed in awesome-mac
caveats: Not notarized by Apple; first launch needs right-click Open or running an xattr quarantine command
Cannot set video on the Lock Screen, since macOS only allows that through its own wallpaper system
